problem: LLMs falter on structured reasoning over relational (tables) and graph-structured data because they must ground entities, compose symbolic constraints, and follow logical paths.
method: STRuCT-LLM jointly trains an LLM on Text-to-SQL and Text-to-Cypher with RL plus Chain-of-Thought supervision, using a topology-aware reward based on graph edit distance. It exploits shared abstractions between SQL and Cypher to induce cross-formalism transfer, and evaluates zero-shot generalization on downstream QA.
key_assumptions: SQL and Cypher share abstractions (schema grounding, filtering, joins, path composition) that permit cross-formalism transfer even without shared schemas.
Executable queries are effective scaffolds for structured reasoning.
RL with CoT supervision plus LLM-judge/execution rewards is a workable training signal.
Graph edit distance is an appropriate topology-aware reward.
main_contribution: A unified RL + CoT framework for structured semantic parsing over tables and graphs with a topology-aware reward, demonstrating cross-formalism transfer and zero-shot downstream generalization without QA-specific supervision; code released.
results: QwQ-32B improves Spider by 13.5% and Text2Cypher by 73.1%; zero-shot downstream gains on TableBench (+8.5%) and CR-LT-KGQA (+1.7%) with no QA-specific supervision.
limitations: Largest results use a 32B model (QwQ-32B), a heavy compute footprint for a full RL pipeline.
No hop-depth analysis; downstream KGQA gain is small (+1.7%).
Transfer is across query formalisms, not across reasoning depth.
Depends on executable-query supervision, which multi-hop KGQA over incomplete KGs may not provide.
code_availability: Code available (paper states: https://github.com/bouv/STRuCT-LLM); repository could not be inspected (GitHub tools unavailable in this investigation).

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: STRuCT-LLM's transfer is cross-formalism (SQL training improving Cypher, and vice versa), not shallow-hop to deep-hop transfer; its supervision is executable query programs, not KG triples/paths enriched with same-passage context. It provides the closest evidence that RL over graph tasks yields zero-shot downstream KGQA gains, but does not test context-enriched supervision or a repair loop.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap moderate: graph-structured reasoning with LLMs, shared interest in RL. Method overlap moderate: RL + CoT supervision and graph-aware rewards, but no context-subgraph supervision. Evaluation overlap low-moderate: downstream KGQA is only a zero-shot side metric (CR-LT-KGQA +1.7%), not the benchmark suite of the idea.
